materialFindings.title: The positive timeout vector cannot distinguish a validated but ignored probeTimeoutMs option
materialFindings.observationGap: The written vectors reject 0/-1/nonfinite and accept explicit 5000, identical to the schema default. They never vary a valid timeout or require observing the forwarded bound. A provider can retain every validation and always use 5000, preserving all those observations while ignoring a positive caller value. Neither RUNNER_SELECT nor executable-selector clauses adds a timeout observation.
materialFindings.requiredRevision: Add distinct valid nondefault A/B timeout vectors with an authenticated future observation of the exact bound passed into the applicable default probe boundary (and the omitted default); distinguish validated-but-ignored/hardcoded timeout. Name any unavailable observation seam as pending instead of assuming private exports. This requests documentary changes only, no execution or new public hook.

materialFindings.title: The probeWindowsAcl binding lacks an observable positive/negative arbitration case
materialFindings.observationGap: The binding names only RUNNER_SELECT. Its concrete vectors exercise Linux rungs, sole-candidate zero calls and cache reuse. Sole Windows selection deliberately bypasses this hook, and ENV_FACTS observes metadata rather than hook influence. Although the prose universally mentions custom chains, no Windows multi-chain vector/count/result distinguishes an ignored hook or constant-partial Windows probe. The selector-specific clauses cover other knobs and do not close this field.
materialFindings.requiredRevision: Write an explicit trusted custom multi-candidate Windows-rung case varying probeWindowsAcl true/false; observe exact invocation count, partial on true, fallthrough/unavailable on false and cached reuse. Retain the separate sole-Windows zero-call case. Bind the case to this leaf and keep fixture/export/native limitations. No native execution or public hook is authorized.
